definition: The standard audio representation: a time-frequency image with frequencies warped to the perceptual mel scale.
details: The standard audio representation: a time-frequency image with frequencies warped to the perceptual mel scale. The input to most ASR encoders and the classic intermediate output of TTS acoustic models.

explainer.lead: The standard audio representation: a time-frequency image whose frequency axis is warped to the perceptual mel scale. It is the input to most speech recognition encoders and the classic intermediate output of text-to-speech acoustic models.

tiers.eli5: A picture of a sound where the vertical axis is pitch arranged the way human ears notice pitch, and the horizontal axis is time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers feed mel spectrograms to ASR encoders and read them as the intermediate output of TTS acoustic models.
tiers.paperLevel: A time-frequency representation of audio with frequencies warped to the perceptual mel scale; it is the standard input to most ASR encoders and the classic intermediate output of TTS acoustic models.

explainer.example: An audio clip is converted into a mel spectrogram image, which is then passed to a speech recognition encoder.
